title: ACT Scores: The 1–36 Composite & How to Lift It
summary: How the ACT composite is built, what's a strong score, and the retake and superscore tactics that raise it.

nodes.label: Percentiles
nodes.note: How you rank vs other test-takers

chunks.heading: How the composite is built
chunks.body: Each core section (**English, Math, Reading**) is scored **1–36**, and your **Composite is their average, rounded** to a whole number. **Science** (and **Writing**) are reported separately, not in the Composite under the updated scoring.
chunks.realExample: English 30, Math 27, Reading 33 → average 30 → Composite 30. Science, if taken, shows as its own 1–36 score plus a STEM score.
chunks.memoryHook: Composite = round(average of English, Math, Reading). Science/Writing separate.

chunks.heading: What's a strong score?
chunks.body: Judge by **percentile and your target colleges**, not a fixed bar. Very roughly, the **national average is around 19–20**, **~26+ is competitive** for many universities, and **~32+ for highly selective** ones. Always check each college's **middle-50% ACT range**.
chunks.realExample: A 30 is strong for many universities but mid-pack at the most selective — look up your target colleges' published middle-50% range to see where you actually stand.
chunks.memoryHook: ~20 average, ~26+ competitive, ~32+ selective — but check each college's own range.

chunks.heading: No penalty — answer everything
chunks.body: There's **no penalty for wrong answers**, so **never leave a blank**. On any section, if time is short, put a 'letter of the day' on every unanswered question — random guesses will win some points, blanks win none.
chunks.realExample: One minute left with eight questions unread? Bubble the same letter for all eight — statistically you'll pick up a couple of points you'd otherwise lose to blanks.
chunks.memoryHook: No penalty. Fill every bubble — a 'letter of the day' beats blanks.

chunks.heading: Retake and superscore
chunks.body: You can **retake the ACT**, and many colleges **superscore** — combining your **best section scores across test dates**. So a focused retake to lift your weakest section can raise your effective Composite without re-acing the others.
chunks.realExample: First ACT: English 32 / Math 25 / Reading 31. A retake lifting Math to 30 gives a superscore Composite around 31 — target your weakest section for the biggest gain.
chunks.memoryHook: Retakes + superscoring = target your weakest section to lift the Composite.

recall.q: How is the ACT Composite calculated?
recall.a: It's the average of English, Math and Reading (each 1–36), rounded to a whole number — Science and Writing are separate.

recall.q: Roughly what ACT scores count as average, competitive and selective?
recall.a: Around 20 is average, ~26+ is competitive for many universities, and ~32+ for highly selective ones — but check each college's middle-50% range.

recall.q: Is there a penalty for wrong answers on the ACT?
recall.a: No — so you should answer every question, using a 'letter of the day' guess if time runs out.

recall.q: What is superscoring on the ACT?
recall.a: Many colleges combine your best section scores across different test dates into a higher Composite.

recall.q: What's the fastest way to raise your Composite on a retake?
recall.a: Focus on lifting your weakest section, since superscoring keeps your already-strong sections.
